title: Safe Interior Compartment Condition (Overhead Close-up)
prompt:
1) Function (1 sentence)
Create a forensic-quality overhead color photograph documenting the condition of a safe’s interior compartment.

2) Scene / Composition (3–5 sentences; include subject percentage in frame)
Single still image of an open safe interior compartment viewed straight down, showing the compartment floor and lower walls with clear surface condition and any residue/dust patterns. The safe interior occupies ~80% of the frame; the remaining ~20% shows a narrow border of the safe frame/lip for context. Include a small, plain, unbranded forensic scale (black-and-white, centimeter ticks) placed along the lower edge of the compartment floor without covering key details. Add minimal annotation as unobtrusive evidence markers: two small white tent markers labeled “A” and “B” near distinct features (e.g., a scratch and a small cluster of debris) without introducing any logos or case text.

3) Angle & Distance (strict numeric values)
Angle: 90.0° overhead (orthographic top-down); distance_m: 0.55 m from lens to compartment floor.

4) Optics & Technique (lens mm, f/, 1/x s, ISO, WB K, focus, DOF)
Lens: 50 mm; aperture: f/8; shutter: 1/125 s; ISO 200; white balance: 5600K. Focus locked on the compartment floor center; deep depth of field so the entire compartment floor and the scale are sharp. Lighting: forensic flash, diffuse and even, minimal shadowing, neutral color rendering.

5) Mandatory elements (labels/markers/timestamps already present in the case)
No timestamps, camera labels, facility labels, or pre-existing identifiers are included (none provided in case context).

6) Negatives (objective list of what MUST NOT appear)
No people, hands, faces, reflections of a person, or identifiable biometrics. No real brand names, logos, serial numbers, official seals/badges, or readable case/evidence IDs inside the image. No weapons, drugs, blood, gore, or graphic violence. No added dates/times, no new labels like camera IDs, zone IDs, door IDs, or location names.

7) Acceptance checklist (objective, verifiable bullets)
- Overhead 90° top-down view with edges of the compartment parallel to the frame
- Safe interior compartment occupies ~80% of the image with a narrow border of the safe lip visible
- Forensic flash lighting is even and color-neutral; no harsh shadows
- Plain black-and-white centimeter scale is visible and legible, not covering key details
- Two small evidence tent markers labeled only “A” and “B” are present and unobtrusive
- No timestamps, no logos/brands, no serial numbers, no people/biometrics, no graphic content
